data.finalText:
I'll start by reading the epic, the PRD and architecture sections, and the workspace layout.
The integration test file wasn't picked up by the filter (its test names don't contain "usb"). I'll run it by file.
Build is progressing. Meanwhile, the tasks file and docs.
While that builds: the docs.
The APK built. Checking for warnings in that run, then copying, hashing and inspecting it.
The APK is arm64-only with targetSdk 36 and the expected permissions. Next I'll confirm minSdk and the merged service and USB filter, run the Kotlin JVM tests, and run the full Rust suite.
Manifest is as designed: `PollingService` is `connectedDevice` (0x10) and not exported, cleartext and backup are off, and the USB attach filter is in place. Now the Kotlin JVM tests:
All 7 Kotlin tests pass. Build outputs aren't ignored, though, and the 182 MB APK shouldn't end up in git by accident. I'll look at what got generated under the plugin before adding ignore rules.
The ignore rules work: only source and config files show as untracked. Next, the full checks plus the write-path guard hook on the new files.
A `buslink-sim --test models` test failed. Let me see which one and why.
After relinking, `models` passes (6/6). One more full workspace run for a clean result, plus the write-guard hook on the new Rust and Kotlin files:
Several files went in through shell heredocs, which skip the PreToolUse guard. I'll replay each new or changed source file through the guard as a full write.
The guard passes on every new and changed file. Last, re-checking the desktop shell after the final edits, including the `e2e` feature build that shares the export path:
`cargo fmt` added about 20 more changed lines in `src-tauri/src`. I'll make sure it didn't restyle code outside this task.
`cargo fmt` touched hunks I didn't edit (the `wizard_*` functions in `control.rs`, and lines 54 and 97 in `state.rs`). Let me see what changed there.
`control.rs` now holds only my change, and clippy is clean on both crates. `lib.rs` wasn't clean at HEAD either, so I'll check that the formatter didn't touch other lines there.
`lib.rs` contains only my changes. Last step: record the APK hash in the docs and fix the date I wrote in `android-build.md` (the build ran on 2026-11-12).
E6 `android-otg` is built and all 7 spec tasks are marked `[x]`. The debug APK builds for arm64, and every test and check passes. None of it has been tried on the A35 yet: installing the APK, the USB permission dialog, the foreground service, polling with the screen off, unplugging the adapter and saving through SAF all still need the manual hardware test.

**APK:** `release/BusLink-Studio-0.1.0-android-arm64-debug.apk`, 182 MB, SHA-256 `735ec1001c4c4b9f4ecbc3791f11fe54913580b15ccf691ca8229b46c6e95e8b` (also in `release/SHA256SUMS.txt`). Reading the built APK confirms:
- package `id.co.arkamaya.buslink`, minSdk 24, targetSdk 36, arm64-v8a only;
- the polling service is type `connectedDevice` and not exported;
- cleartext traffic and backup are off, and the USB attach filter is included.

It is signed with the debug key only. JDK 23 worked with this Gradle version, so I changed nothing in the toolchain. The `.apk` is git-ignored; the hash file is kept.

**What was added**
- **Spec:** `.kiro/specs/android-otg/` with requirements, design (correctness properties A1–A9) and tasks.
- **Buffering adapter (Rust core):** `transport/usb.rs` turns USB packets into the byte stream the RTU parser expects. It holds the rest of a large packet for the next read, keeps merged packets in order, returns zero bytes on timeout, and fails every read and write after a detach. It also includes a fake USB port for tests.
- **Plugin `plugins/tauri-plugin-buslink-usb`:**
  - The Rust side exposes no command to the webview and no write command.
  - The Kotlin side uses usb-serial-for-android 3.12.0 to list devices, request permission and open/read/write/close ports.
  - Permission: one request at a time, 60 s timeout, cancelled on unplug or when the app leaves the screen, no repeated prompts.
  - Unplugging the adapter closes the port and stops the service.
  - Also included: the `connectedDevice` service with its notification (en/id), the notification permission request, and the SAF save.
- **App:** `android_usb.rs` and `files.rs` are new.
  - Connect, port listing and Start polling now run off the main thread, so the permission dialog can answer.
  - Android links wait at least 50 ms between frames.
  - The service starts only from Start polling while the app is open. It stops when no real link is polling, and on app exit.
  - The save dialog plugin is now desktop-only.
- **UI:** Android battery/OTG note, "permission needed" in the port list, a warning above 115 200 baud, and an honest message if polling won't continue with the screen off.
- **Android project:** generated with `tauri android init`. I edited `targetSdk` to 36, turned cleartext off in debug, scoped JitPack to usb-serial-for-android, and added the manifest entries and `device_filter.xml`. Every edit is listed in `docs/android-build.md`.
- **Docs:** `docs/verification/android-hardware.md` has 15 steps and empty result cells for you. Disclosure rows 15–17 record what I learned from Soil-Sensor-Android; no code was copied. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` has a new Android section.

**Checks**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace` | 223 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` | clean |
| `cargo.exe check` / `clippy -D warnings` (app, `e2e` feature, plugin) | clean |
| `cargo.exe test --lib` (app) | 2 passed |
| Kotlin JVM tests (`PacketQueueTest`) | 7 passed |
| `tsc`, i18n check, UI check, `node --test` | pass (570 keys, 18 tests) |
| Hook self-tests | 89 OK |
| `guard_writes.py` on every new or changed file | no block |

**Problems hit and fixed**
- The first APK build failed because of my plugin code: it needed androidx.core 1.13.1. The Gradle "different roots" warning in the log is harmless; Gradle falls back by itself.
- One test binary (`buslink-sim/tests/models`) crashed even when only listing its tests, so the file on the D: drive was damaged. After rebuilding it, it passed 6/6.
- Windows `cargo.exe fmt` ignores the repo's `rustfmt.toml` and reformatted code I hadn't touched in `control.rs`. I restored that file to HEAD plus only my change.

**Follow-up**
- Run the hardware procedure on the A35, then decide whether to add an Android evidence entry to the soil sensor profile.
- The APK was built just before final formatting-only edits (no logic changes); rebuild before installing it on the phone.
- The time cost of one Rust↔Kotlin call per USB packet hasn't been measured; step 7 of the procedure records it.
- `tauri android dev` needs the debug cleartext setting switched back to `true` locally.

Nothing was committed or pushed.
